title: RemoteEvent.OnServerEvent
summary: Server-side event that fires when ANY client calls FireServer. The firing Player is automatically the first callback parameter — guaranteed authentic by the engine, unspoofable.

parameters.name: player
parameters.description: Injected by Roblox — the exact Player whose client called FireServer. Cannot be spoofed. Always first.

parameters.name: ...args
parameters.description: Exactly the arguments the client passed, in order. Client-controlled: always validate.

details.heading: Where it works
details.body: Server only (Scripts). Connecting it in a LocalScript never fires — client reception is OnClientEvent.

details.heading: Security posture
details.body: The player identity is trustworthy; everything after it is not. Rate-limit per player and type/range-check arguments before acting.

explanation.whatItIs: The server's doorbell for client messages — and it always announces exactly who rang.
explanation.whyItExists: Multiplayer games live here: every legitimate client action funnels through OnServerEvent handlers with a verified actor attached.
whenToUse: Every client → server interaction: buying, building, abilities, chat commands
Central dispatch with a command-string first argument
tips: Connect handlers at server startup, BEFORE clients can fire
Validate in this exact order: identity (given) → types → ranges → cooldowns → game rules
One remote + dispatch table scales better than dozens of remotes
commonMistakes: Writing the callback WITHOUT the leading player parameter — every argument shifts and logic silently misreads
Trusting arguments: `local amount = args[1]` applied directly = exploiters printing money
Connecting in a LocalScript and debugging forever why nothing happens

examples.title: The player parameter, demonstrated
examples.code:
-- Client fires:
-- remote:FireServer("Heal", 50)

-- Server receives:
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, action, amount)
    --                  ↑ Roblox adds this!  ↑ client's arg 1  ↑ client's arg 2
    if typeof(action) ~= "string" then return end
    if typeof(amount) ~= "number" then return end

    if action == "Heal" then
        local humanoid = player.Character and player.Character:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
        if humanoid then
            humanoid.Health = math.min(humanoid.MaxHealth, humanoid.Health + amount)
        end
    end
end)
examples.whyItWorks: The engine supplies `player` — the handler knows WHO wants healing without the client ever sending identity data. The amount is still client-controlled, so a real game would cap/rate-limit it.
examples.commonMistake: Omitting `player` from the signature: function(action, amount) makes action receive the Player object instead of "Heal".
